excerpt: Prove identity / Who are you → Authentication
actual: Final cheat sheet assigns the identification question to Authentication.
expected: Who are you/claim identity maps to Identification; prove identity maps to Authentication.
rootCause: One mnemonic row combines two separately defined access-control stages.
evidence: D1:174–176 and 238 distinguish claiming identity from proving it; D1:1307 contradicts that distinction.
recommendation: Split Identification and Authentication into separate rows.

excerpt: ปัจจัยการพิสูจน์ตัวตนแบ่งออกเป็น 4 หมวดหลัก
actual: Location is presented beside independent MFA factors; generated card calls it contextual without excluding it from satisfying MFA.
expected: Knowledge, possession and inherence are independent factor types; location is a supplementary risk/context signal.
rootCause: The four-category heading and contextual card are combined under the independent-factor MFA definition.
evidence: D1:187–195 and content-components.js:60–69; SP 800-63B-4 says fraud indicators cannot substitute for an authentication factor.
recommendation: Separate location context and add password plus corporate IP is not MFA.
confidence: high for misleading scope; medium for exam consequence

excerpt: Threat คือสิ่งภายนอก
actual: Warnings define threats as external, despite earlier malicious-insider example.
expected: Threats can originate internally or externally; distinguish potential harm from exploitable weakness.
rootCause: External/internal is used as the defining threat-versus-vulnerability distinction.
evidence: D1:21 correctly lists malicious insiders; D1:37 and 1040 restrict threats to external sources.
recommendation: Remove external-only wording and include an insider example.

excerpt: ที่เปิดโอกาสให้ Threat ถูกใช้ประโยชน์
actual: Thai passive grammar says that the threat is exploited.
expected: Threat sources exploit vulnerabilities.
rootCause: The passive object in the Thai definition is Threat rather than the weakness.
evidence: D1:22 reverses the exploitation relationship; later D1 material generally uses the correct relationship.
recommendation: Use จุดอ่อน...ที่ภัยคุกคามหรือผู้ก่อภัยคุกคามอาจใช้ประโยชน์เพื่อก่อความเสียหาย.

excerpt: Controller/Processor ทั่วโลกที่มีการประมวลผลข้อมูลพลเมืองสหภาพยุโรป
actual: GDPR applicability is described as processing EU citizens' data anywhere.
expected: Applicability depends on Article 3 establishment and targeting criteria; citizenship alone is not the test.
rootCause: Citizenship is substituted for territorial-scope criteria.
evidence: EDPB Guidelines 3/2018 explain that nationality does not determine Article 3(2) targeting applicability.
recommendation: Replace citizenship rule with concise qualified establishment/targeting language.

excerpt: Audit Trails, ประทับเวลา (Timestamps) ... (Non-Repudiation)
actual: Mobile AAA diagram implies ordinary timestamped logs create non-repudiation.
expected: Logs support accountability; non-repudiation requires appropriate evidence and assurance controls.
rootCause: Accounting text assigns a stronger property than ordinary logging establishes.
evidence: DG:464 contrasts with D1:250's signed-evidence discussion; NIST digital-signature definition qualifies assurance by appropriate use.
recommendation: Label logging as accountability and separately explain non-repudiation evidence requirements.

excerpt: ต้นทุนของมาตรการความปลอดภัยต่อปีไม่ควรเกินมูลค่า ALE
actual: Prose and desktop compare control costs with entire ALE; mobile compares them with ALE savings.
expected: Compare annual costs with expected ALE reduction, while recognizing legal/safety/contract constraints.
rootCause: Desktop/prose omit residual ALE while mobile uses risk reduction.
evidence: D1:505–506 and DG:744 differ from DG:795. If ALE falls from $10,000 to $9,000 at $5,000 annual cost, being below total ALE does not make the control economical.
recommendation: Use ALE before minus ALE after and align both layouts; qualify the economic rule.

excerpt: เช่น NIST ... Identify → Assess → Treat → Monitor
actual: Callout attributes this named four-stage sequence to NIST and claims ISC2 explicitly mandates a fifth reporting stage.
expected: NIST SP 800-39 uses Frame, Assess, Respond, Monitor; label local five-stage mnemonic as pedagogical unless official course source is supplied.
rootCause: The named NIST sequence in the local callout differs from the primary source.
evidence: NIST CSF FAQ and SP 800-39 confirm Frame/Assess/Respond/Monitor. Public ISC2 outline does not establish the separate fifth-stage claim; that part remains unverified attribution.
recommendation: Correct NIST attribution and cite official training source or label five-stage model as local teaching structure.
confidence: high for NIST mismatch; qualified for ISC2 training claim

excerpt: ลำดับคำใน Canon 2 ให้เกียรติและความซื่อสัตย์มาก่อนกฎหมาย
actual: Text infers priority of honesty over legality from adjective order inside Canon 2.
expected: Treat those duties together; lawful conduct may still be unethical without implying word-order precedence.
rootCause: Lexical order is interpreted as a normative hierarchy without a supporting source.
evidence: ISC2 public code provides the duties together and no adjective hierarchy.
recommendation: Remove lexical-precedence interpretation; retain lawful-but-unethical example.

excerpt: อาจมีความผิดฐาน Gross Negligence ... ซึ่งไม่ได้รับการคุ้มครองทางกฎหมาย
actual: Mobile diagram asserts categorical absence of legal protection after potential gross negligence.
expected: Describe possible professional/legal consequences without a jurisdiction-free immunity rule.
evidence: DG:1280 qualifies possible gross negligence with may, but not the final loss-of-protection clause. ISC2 Code establishes ethical duties, not the asserted universal legal rule; no particular country's negligence law was validated.
recommendation: Use qualified negligence/liability language and professional discipline; omit universal loss-of-protection conclusion.

excerpt: เอกสารรวบรวมและเรียบเรียงเนื้อหาฉบับสมบูรณ์
actual: No AI/training-data/model-poisoning applications appear in this Domain 1 material.
expected: Include concise foundational examples reflecting current ISC2 web guidance.
evidence: Full reading and targeted search found no such examples. ISC2 current page explains Domain 1 AI applications; all five formal objective labels are otherwise covered.
recommendation: Add short CIA, privacy/AAA, risk/governance and ethics examples; no new AI domain required.

excerpt: แจ้งเตือนภัยแบบเรียลไทม์ขณะที่เหตุการณ์หรือการโจมตีกำลังดำเนินอยู่
actual: Main diagram restricts Detective to during/real time and correction to after incident, despite an overlap caption.
expected: Classify primarily by purpose; detective controls also identify prior events and correction can overlap active response.
evidence: DG:1053–1084,1125–1129,1140; mitigating overlap caption DG:1177–1179 acknowledged. D1:851 correctly calls retrospective CCTV detective; CISA guide p.13 supports retrospective investigations.
recommendation: Use often-before/during/after labels, add delayed detection, and identify absent directive/compensating functions as cross-cutting or title diagram selected functions.

excerpt: ขจัดจุดล้มเหลวเดี่ยว (No Single Point of Failure)
actual: Diagram lists seven defenses around an isolated core and implies adding layers eliminates single failure points; layer 6 Thai grammar suggests preventing encryption.
expected: Show complementary relationship to core; describe reducing reliance on one control and use Thai wording protecting data through encryption.
evidence: DG:565–605 has lists and core without connections/enclosing layers; DG:610 overstates elimination; DG:676 wording ป้องกันช่องโหว่ซอฟต์แวร์และการเข้ารหัสข้อมูล is awkward. Seven layers are explicitly an example and defensible.
recommendation: Connect/surround layers; qualify independence/diversity and eliminate overpromise; change layer 6 wording to ปกป้องข้อมูลด้วยการเข้ารหัส.

excerpt: Risk ... ผลรวมของโอกาส ... ควบคู่กับขนาดของผลกระทบ
actual: Thai sum wording and residual-risk subtraction appear alongside a multiplicative mnemonic without model assumptions.
expected: Use combination; label likelihood×impact and subtraction as simplified models requiring defined compatible scales.
evidence: D1:388,409,580,1056–1060. Approximation sign in risk formula and correct before/after definitions partially mitigate concern.
recommendation: Reassess remaining likelihood and consequence; avoid arithmetic on ordinal High/Medium/Low labels.

excerpt: การจัดเก็บ (Collection)
actual: Collection translation overlaps storage; controller definition excludes natural persons; consent flow can imply universality; tax retention example lacks jurisdiction.
expected: Translate Collection as การเก็บรวบรวม; include natural-person controllers; qualify consent as one legal basis; source jurisdiction-specific retention.
evidence: D1:256,267,281,291 and DG:521,533. EDPB supports natural/legal person roles and multiple lawful bases. Seven-year Thai employee-tax rule was not verified; erasure exception is appropriately qualified.
recommendation: Clarify translation, roles and applicable lawful basis; source or label the retention assumption.

excerpt: รหัสผ่านต้องมีความยาวอย่างน้อย 14 ตัวอักษร ผสมอักขระ 3 ใน 4 ประเภท
actual: Hypothetical password standard teaches dated composition rules; security questions lack legacy labeling; diagram says standards have no exceptions.
expected: Use modern example with length/blocklist/MFA and clarify organization-defined scope and approved exceptions.
evidence: D1:683, content-components.js:37, DG:1001,1012. NIST SP 800-63B-4 §3.1.1 prohibits composition rules in that standard. Hypothetical example still correctly illustrates a measurable standard.
recommendation: Replace dated example, label security questions legacy, and qualify mandatory/no-exception language.
confidence: high about NIST divergence; medium about hypothetical example harm

excerpt: การลง Patch อุดช่องโหว่ทันทีที่ได้รับแจ้ง
actual: Immediate installation is presented as due care without change/risk context; scanning-all-servers scenario omits explicit authorization.
expected: Teach authorized risk-based normal/emergency change process and prudent response.
evidence: D1:917,1258,1267; scenarios 4 and 5; DG:1206,1252. Expected Due Diligence/Due Care answers remain correct.
recommendation: Add authorized scan scope and approved/emergency patch process, verification and urgency context.

excerpt: Canon ลำดับก่อนหน้าจะมีความสำคัญเหนือกว่าเสมอ
actual: Strict inter-canon priority is repeatedly asserted without an accessible official training citation.
expected: Cite official course source or explain as a prioritization aid while preserving professional judgment.
evidence: D1:956–964,977 and DG:1292–1397. Current ISC2 public code gives four canons in same order but omits a strict hierarchy; omission does not prove no official training uses it.
recommendation: Supply traceable training citation or qualify the absolute always-supersedes rule.
confidence: high that public page omits rule; insufficient to declare convention false

excerpt: เกิดขึ้นหลังจาก Authentication สำเร็จแล้วเสมอ
actual: Authorization always after authentication and always-available phrasing overgeneralize; load-balancer example claims elimination of SPOFs with one LB.
expected: Qualify named-user login model and service availability goals; ensure redundant LB tier before claiming full topology eliminates SPOFs.
evidence: D1:115,222; DG:289. Single load balancer source topology does not show redundancy at that tier; anonymous resource authorization is outside the illustrated login model.
recommendation: Use in this authenticated-user flow, timely/reliable service requirements, and explicit redundant LB assumption.

excerpt: Technical / Managerial (Administrative) / Operational / Physical
actual: Four-bucket taxonomy is presented without mapping to official three-category outline; Thai mantrap label has typo.
expected: Explain operational bucket as an alternative taxonomy/extension and map to technical, administrative and physical.
evidence: D1:758–763; content-components.js:182–218. Official outline names technical/admin/physical; operational controls are legitimate in other taxonomies. CC:217 contains ประตูกลักกันคนเดินตาม.
recommendation: Map categories explicitly and correct Thai access-control-vestibule label.
